name: Okta

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Okta logo (2023).svg, the en.wikipedia.org Okta infobox logo, in use since 2022)

description: Okta sells cloud identity software: it makes sure the right person (or, increasingly, software agent) can log in to the right application. Its Okta Platform serves 'workforce identity' (employees, contractors and partners: single sign-on, multi-factor login, identity governance, privileged access) and its Auth0 Platform lets developers build login into their own customer-facing apps ('customer identity'). More than 20,000 customers pay a subscription (98% of revenue), invoiced mostly annually in advance and driven by the number of customers, users per customer and products used; remaining contracted revenue was $4.8 billion at January 2026. Revenue grew 12% to $2.92 billion in fiscal 2026 and the company turned GAAP-profitable (operating income $149 million, net income $235 million), and it now buys back stock under a $1 billion program.

gics.note: Listed as Information Technology / Application Software in Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies' (raw wikitext read 2026-10-27); Okta joined the S&P MidCap 400 in 2025 (same page's change log). The list gives sector and sub-industry only, so industry group and industry are left null rather than recalled. Not in the S&P 500 list. EDGAR SIC (submissions record): 7372 Services-Prepackaged Software.

employees.note: About 56% in the United States and 44% international (FY2026 10-K Item 1).

businessLines.name: Okta Platform (workforce identity and customer identity)
businessLines.how: Subscription fees for access to and use of the cloud platform plus support, invoiced mostly annually in advance; driven by the number of customers, users per customer and solutions used. Land-and-expand: 5,100 customers pay more than $100,000 a year.
businessLines.description: Workforce products (Single Sign-On, Adaptive MFA, Universal Directory, Lifecycle Management, Identity Governance, Privileged Access, Access Gateway, Identity Threat Protection and Okta for AI Agents in early access) plus customer-identity use of the same platform.

businessLines.name: Auth0 Platform (customer identity for developers)
businessLines.how: Subscription fees on the same company-wide basis (customers, users per customer, solutions used); the 10-K does not describe a separate Auth0 pricing unit.
businessLines.description: Developer-focused identity: Universal Login, Private Cloud deployment, Organizations for B2B customers, Attack Protection Suite, extensibility (Actions, Forms, Event Streams) and the Auth0 Marketplace.

businessLines.name: Professional services and other
businessLines.how: One-time fees for configuration, deployment plans and expert assistance, sold to help customers adopt the subscriptions; it runs at a loss.
businessLines.description: Fees for implementing and optimizing customers' deployments.
